text: The LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised.
Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the very time God had spoken of.
Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son born to him, the son Sarah bore him.

versions.text: Abraham named the son born to him, whom Sarah bore him, Isaac.
versions.explanation: The current word order delays the name to the very end after two relative clauses, which is hard to follow when read aloud. Fronting the name and simplifying the second clause preserves the Hebrew content while improving oral flow.

text: And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

Then Sarah said, "God has brought me laughter; everyone who hears will laugh with me."[^1]

[^1]: The name Isaac sounds like the Hebrew word for 'he laughs'.

versions.text: Then Sarah said, "God has brought me laughter; everyone who hears will laugh with me."
versions.explanation: A brief footnote on the wordplay between Isaac's name and 'laughter' helps hearers catch the point of the verse, which is otherwise invisible in English.

text: And she said, "Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age."
The child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
But Sarah saw the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham mocking,
and she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit along with my son, with Isaac."
This troubled Abraham deeply, because of his son.
But God said to Abraham, "Do not be troubled about the boy and about your slave woman. Listen to whatever Sarah says to you, for through Isaac your offspring shall be named.
And I will also make a nation of the slave woman's son, because he is your offspring."

So Abraham rose early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water and gave them to Hagar, placing them on her shoulder, and he sent her away with the boy. She went off and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes
and went and sat down a good way off, about a bowshot away, for she said, "Let me not watch the boy die." And as she sat there, she lifted up her voice and wept.
God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, "What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.

versions.text: God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, "What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.
versions.explanation: בַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא־שָׁם means simply 'where he is'; 'where he lies' adds a posture not stated in the Hebrew.

text: Get up, lift the boy and hold him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation."
Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
God was with the boy, and he grew up. He lived in the wilderness and became an archer.
He settled in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
At that time Abimelech, together with Phicol the commander of his army, said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do.

Now swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me or with my offspring or with my posterity. Show to me and to the land where you have lived as a foreigner the same kindness I have shown to you.

versions.text: Now swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me or with my children or with my descendants. Show to me and to the land where you have lived as a foreigner the same kindness I have shown to you."
versions.explanation: נִין and נֶכֶד denote descendants of later generations (grandchildren and great-grandchildren), not 'children'. 'Offspring... posterity' better reflects the pairing.

text: And Abraham said, "I swear it."
Then Abraham confronted Abimelech about the well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized.
Abimelech said, "I do not know who did this. You never told me, and I heard nothing of it until today."
So Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.
Abraham also set apart seven ewe lambs from the flock,
and Abimelech asked him, "What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs you have set apart?"
He answered, "Accept these seven ewe lambs from my hand as my witness that I dug this well."
That is why the place was called Beersheba, because there the two of them swore an oath.
When they had made the covenant at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army set out and returned to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree at Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
And Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for a long time.
